articles.title: Google Cloud Posts 82% Revenue Surge as Kerala-Born CEO Thomas Kurian Cements AI Dominance
articles.excerpt: Alphabet's cloud division generated $24.8 billion in Q2 2026, far exceeding analyst expectations of 63% growth, as enterprise demand for AI infrastructure accelerated under the leadership of Indian-American executive Thomas Kurian.
articles.image_caption: Thomas Kurian, CEO of Google Cloud, has led the division since 2019. Under his leadership, Google Cloud revenue has grown from roughly $8.9 billion annually to a $99 billion annualized run rate.
articles.nri_angle: Thomas Kurian, born in Pampady, Kerala, is one of the most prominent Indian-origin CEOs in Silicon Valley. His twin brother George Kurian serves as CEO of NetApp, making them one of tech's most notable Indian-American sibling duos.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Blackstone Earnings Surge 26% as AI Bets Power Record $1.35 Trillion Empire
articles.excerpt: The world's largest alternative asset manager beat Wall Street estimates handily, with nine of its top 10 best-performing investments linked to artificial intelligence.
articles.image_caption: Stephen Schwarzman, chairman and CEO of Blackstone. The firm reported a 26% earnings surge in Q2 2026 as AI-driven data center investments powered its growth to $1.35 trillion in assets.
articles.nri_angle: Blackstone listed its Bagmane office REIT in Bengaluru — the most oversubscribed REIT IPO in India's history — and its accelerating global data center buildout has implications for India's tech workforce and growing data center industry.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft and Amazon Chart Divergent Paths in the Battle for Cloud Gaming
articles.excerpt: Xbox begins testing ad-supported game streaming for Insiders, while Amazon bets on bundling Luna with Prime to reach billions of casual players who don't own consoles.
articles.image_caption: Xbox's promotional graphic for its new ad-supported cloud gaming test, launched July 23 for Xbox Insiders. Microsoft and Amazon are pursuing contrasting strategies to make cloud gaming accessible to players without dedicated hardware.
articles.nri_angle: India's cloud gaming market — where Xbox starts at ₹499/month and Luna is free with Prime — offers the diaspora affordable access to console-quality games without expensive hardware investments.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: EU Hits Google With $1 Billion Fine as US Threatens Tariff Retaliation
articles.excerpt: The European Commission fined Alphabet's Google €890 million for breaching the Digital Markets Act — the tech giant's first penalties under the landmark law — as U.S. lawmakers call for trade retaliation over Europe's tech regulations.
articles.image_caption: Teresa Ribera, the European Commission's executive vice president for competition policy, announced the €890 million fine against Google. The decision marks the first DMA penalties for the tech giant amid rising U.S.-EU trade tensions.
articles.nri_angle: EU tech regulation sets precedent that could affect Indian IT companies operating in Europe and shapes the global regulatory landscape for Big Tech.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Framework Unveils 192 GB Desktop PC Built to Run AI Models Locally
articles.excerpt: The compact mini-ITX system, powered by AMD's Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 495, can run DeepSeek V4-Flash at Q8 quantization on a single box — no discrete GPU required.
articles.image_caption: The Framework Desktop with AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 495 and 192 GB of unified memory displayed alongside a monitor at AMD's Advancing AI 2026 event. The system is designed to run large language models locally without a discrete GPU.
articles.nri_angle: Indian AI developers and startups could benefit from affordable local inference hardware as cloud compute costs and data sovereignty concerns grow.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ServiceNow Invests $40 Million in India's BusinessNext at $700 Million Valuation
articles.excerpt: The strategic deal gives the Noida-based banking software firm access to ServiceNow's global sales network as it pushes into AI-powered autonomous banking.
articles.image_caption: ServiceNow's headquarters building. The U.S. enterprise software company has invested $40 million in Indian banking software firm BusinessNext, valuing it at $700 million.
articles.nri_angle: The investment signals growing global recognition of India's enterprise software capabilities, with BusinessNext expanding its AI-powered banking platform from Indian institutions to markets worldwide including the U.S., Southeast Asia, Australia, and New Zealand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Travis Kalanick's Atoms Raises $1.7 Billion to Build Industrial AI Empire
articles.excerpt: The Uber co-founder's robotics company has secured major backing from Andreessen Horowitz and Uber, with plans to automate mining, food production, and heavy transport.
articles.image_caption: Travis Kalanick, co-founder of Uber and founder of Atoms. The industrial robotics company has raised $1.7 billion in a funding round led by Andreessen Horowitz.
articles.nri_angle: The deal highlights the continued prominence of Indian-origin tech entrepreneurs in Silicon Valley and signals growing demand for engineering talent in the physical AI sector.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pichai Defends Google's AI Strategy as Investors Question Gemini Delays
articles.excerpt: Alphabet's CEO pushed back against Wall Street concerns about falling behind in AI coding, pointing to 82% cloud growth and teasing the ambitious Gemini 4 model during the company's Q2 earnings call.
articles.image_caption: Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai. He mounted a robust defense of Google's AI strategy during the company's Q2 2026 earnings call on Wednesday, addressing investor concerns about delayed model releases.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-born CEO Sundar Pichai faces a pivotal moment defending Google's AI strategy, as the company's performance and strategy have implications for thousands of Indian tech workers in its workforce.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: JPMorgan Plans 1,000 New Tech Hires in India Even as AI Reshapes Its Workforce
articles.excerpt: The Wall Street giant is doubling down on India's Global Capability Centres for AI, cloud, and cybersecurity talent, even as it deploys artificial intelligence to cut jobs by up to 40% in some business units.
articles.image_caption: JPMorgan Chase's headquarters at 270 Park Avenue in New York. The bank is expanding its technology workforce in India even as AI transforms operations across the firm.
articles.nri_angle: Indian tech professionals, including diaspora members considering a return, face growing demand for AI and cloud specialists at JPMorgan's expanding India centres.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Uber Cuts 10% of Customer Service Jobs as AI Overhaul Reshapes Operations
articles.excerpt: The ride-hailing giant is eliminating roughly one in ten customer service roles, citing its growing 'embrace' of artificial intelligence — the latest in a string of workforce restructuring moves that have accompanied Uber's aggressive AI adoption.
articles.image_caption: Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi has acknowledged that AI spending is creating direct trade-offs with headcount at the company. Uber has cut customer service and HR roles in 2026 while aggressively deploying AI tools.
articles.nri_angle: Uber's customer service restructuring has implications for India's large BPO and customer support sector, where the company operates significant support centres employing thousands of workers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Natural Gas Is the Next AI Bottleneck, and Investors Are Racing to Get Ahead of It

articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin tech professionals and investors with AI sector exposure face new risks as energy costs threaten to reshape Big Tech economics.

articles.title: GitHub Scales Back Public Bug Bounties as AI-Generated Reports Overwhelm Program
articles.excerpt: The code platform is replacing cash payouts with swag for low-impact reports and concentrating top rewards in its invitation-only VIP tier, as AI-generated security submissions flood the industry.
articles.image_caption: GitHub headquarters. The company is scaling back its public bug bounty program amid a surge of AI-generated reports (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian cybersecurity researchers are among the top bug bounty earners globally, and stricter entry requirements could affect the talent pipeline.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Extends Solar Cell Sourcing Exemption to December, Buying Time for Domestic Manufacturing
articles.excerpt: The MNRE's six-month extension of the ALMM-II waiver for net metering and open access projects could unlock up to 10 GW of stalled installations, but the gap between module and cell manufacturing capacity remains a structural challenge.
articles.image_caption: Solar panels at the Pavagada Solar Park in Karnataka, one of India's largest solar installations. India has built nearly 200 GW of module manufacturing capacity but domestic cell production remains a fraction of that.
articles.nri_angle: The policy shift affects diaspora investors backing India's clean energy transition and NRI-led solar ventures navigating domestic sourcing requirements.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Pixel Watch 5 Leaks Reveal New Colors, Price Hike Ahead of August Launch
articles.excerpt: Official press renders show four colorways matching the Pixel 11 lineup, while reports point to the first price increase in the smartwatch’s four-year history.
articles.image_caption: A Google Pixel Watch, the predecessor to the upcoming Pixel Watch 5 expected to launch on August 12. Leaked renders show four new colorways matching the Pixel 11 smartphone lineup.
articles.nri_angle: The Pixel Watch 5 is sold in India where Google’s wearable market share remains small, and pricing changes in the US will influence the Indian launch price for the diaspora audience tracking tech purchases across markets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's AI Reckoning: Middle Managers Face Mass Displacement as Companies Flatten Hierarchies
articles.excerpt: From TCS to Oracle, Indian and global firms are eliminating mid-level roles as AI agents replace the coordination work that once justified the managerial layer.
articles.image_caption: India's IT services sector employed millions of middle managers whose coordination roles are now being replaced by AI agents. Industry leaders including TCS chairman N. Chandrasekaran have acknowledged that hiring numbers will shrink as autonomous systems absorb more work.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin professionals in IT and BPM roles across the US, UK, and Gulf states face the same middle-management compression as their counterparts in India, with lateral hiring demand falling sharply.

articles.title: Astronomers Detect First Possible Moon Outside Our Solar System
articles.excerpt: A Jupiter-sized object orbiting a brown dwarf 71 light-years from Earth could be the first exomoon ever found, but the discovery has scientists debating whether existing cosmic labels still apply.
articles.image_caption: An artist's impression of the CD-35 2722 system, showing the newly detected moon-like exosatellite at the center, orbiting a brown dwarf that itself circles a red dwarf star. The discovery, made using ESO's Very Large Telescope, could represent the first detection of a moon-like body outside our solar system.
articles.nri_angle: Indian Institute of Astrophysics researchers in Bangalore have developed exomoon detection models for JWST that could help confirm future candidates like the CD-35 2722 exosatellite.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tesla Profits Plunge as AI Spending Surges and EV Discounts Squeeze Margins
articles.excerpt: Revenue beat expectations on record deliveries, but a 57% drop in operating income and Tesla's first cash burn in over two years rattled investors as Elon Musk doubles down on robotaxis and humanoid robots.
articles.image_caption: Tesla's Gigafactory in Austin, Texas. The company reported record Q2 deliveries but saw profits plunge as AI spending surged and EV discounts squeezed margins.
articles.nri_angle: Tesla's AI and robotics pivot sustains demand for Indian-origin engineering talent, while CFO Vaibhav Taneja is among the most prominent diaspora executives in the global auto industry.

articles.title: Johnson & Johnson Wins FDA Nod for Ottava Surgical Robot
articles.excerpt: The authorisation clears J&J to challenge Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci system in the soft-tissue robotic surgery market with a table-integrated design that takes up half the space.
articles.image_caption: Johnson & Johnson's corporate headquarters. The healthcare conglomerate received FDA marketing authorisation for its Ottava robotic surgical system on July 22, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin surgeons and healthcare professionals in the U.S. represent a significant share of the surgical workforce and will be among the early evaluators of the Ottava system.

articles.title: Google Quadruples Miami Office as Co-Founders Flee California's Billionaire Tax

articles.image_caption: Google's headquarters in Mountain View, California. The tech giant is quadrupling its Miami office space as co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin relocate from California.
articles.nri_angle: The expansion creates new tech employment opportunities in a no-income-tax state while raising questions about California's long-term viability as a hub for diaspora tech founders
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Alphabet's Cloud Boom Powers Record Quarter, but AI Spending Spooks Investors
articles.excerpt: Google's parent company posted $119.8 billion in revenue and 82% cloud growth in Q2, beating Wall Street expectations. But a raised capex forecast of up to $205 billion sent shares sliding after hours.
articles.image_caption: Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai acknowledged the company needs to improve in certain AI areas, even as Google Cloud revenue surged 82% in the second quarter. The company raised its full-year capex forecast to as much as $205 billion.
articles.nri_angle: Alphabet's accelerating cloud growth and AI investment signal sustained demand for Indian IT services and engineering talent in the U.S.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Big Tech's AI Spending Spree Is Eating Into Free Cash Flow, and Investors Are Worried
articles.excerpt: A Reuters analysis shows hyperscalers will spend $1.57 for every $1 of additional cash flow by 2027, as Alphabet kicks off a pivotal earnings season on Wednesday.
articles.image_caption: An NVIDIA AI server rack. U.S. hyperscalers are pouring hundreds of billions into AI infrastructure, raising investor concerns about free cash flow.
articles.nri_angle: Tech stocks dominate many Indian diaspora portfolios and the sector is the largest H-1B employer; a spending-driven valuation reset could affect hiring and Indian IT services demand.

articles.title: Samsung Unveils Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2 With Major Battery Upgrades
articles.excerpt: The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 packs an 800mAh battery — a 35% jump over its predecessor — alongside a new Snapdragon Wear Elite chip and 5,000-nit display brightness.
articles.image_caption: Samsung Galaxy Watch 9, unveiled at Galaxy Unpacked with a 30% larger battery and upgraded Exynos processor.
articles.nri_angle: Samsung's new Galaxy Watch lineup is expected to launch in India within weeks, with health-tracking features like sleep apnea detection catering to the growing wellness market among Indian consumers.

articles.title: Samsung Launches Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, Fold 8, and Flip 8 at Galaxy Unpacked
articles.excerpt: The new Fold 8 Ultra features a 200MP camera, 8-inch inner display, and 5,000mAh battery in a 4.1mm-thin body. Samsung also introduced a new wide-format Fold 8 and its slimmest Flip phone yet.
articles.image_caption: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, launched at Galaxy Unpacked alongside the Fold 8 and Flip 8.
articles.nri_angle: Samsung opened pre-reservations in India ahead of the launch, with the new foldable lineup expected to be priced competitively against Apple's anticipated foldable iPhone.

articles.title: AMD and Anthropic Strike $5 Billion Chip Deal in Major AI Partnership
articles.excerpt: Anthropic will deploy up to 2 gigawatts of AMD's next-generation MI450 GPUs, while AMD commits a strategic equity investment of up to $5 billion in the AI startup.
articles.image_caption: AMD CEO Lisa Su at a technology conference. Su announced the strategic partnership with Anthropic at AMD's Advancing AI 2026 event.
articles.nri_angle: The AMD-Anthropic partnership expands opportunities for Indian-origin engineers and executives in the booming AI semiconductor sector across Silicon Valley.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Utilities Join Trump Pledge to Shield Consumers From AI Power Costs
articles.excerpt: Nearly 200 entities covering 80% of U.S. power delivery have signed on, as Congress advances the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act to prevent data center energy costs from reaching household bills.
articles.image_caption: A data center; U.S. utilities have pledged to shield consumers from rising AI power costs
articles.nri_angle: Rising U.S. electricity costs and potential regulatory slowdowns on data centers affect Indian Americans both as consumers and as a workforce heavily employed in the AI and tech sectors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New Phishing Platforms Bypass Microsoft 365 MFA Using Device Code Attacks
articles.excerpt: Subscription-based phishing kits Forg365 and Kali365, sold on Telegram for as little as $250 a month, are enabling even low-skill attackers to hijack corporate Microsoft 365 accounts by abusing legitimate authentication flows.
articles.image_caption: An illustration of a phishing attack. New platforms are bypassing Microsoft 365 multi-factor authentication using device code attacks.
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT services firms and diaspora professionals managing enterprise Microsoft 365 environments face elevated risk from these industrialised phishing platforms.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Samsung Launches AI Health Assistant as Tech Giants Race to Own Your Wellness Data
articles.excerpt: The AI-powered chatbot, now in beta for US users, analyzes sleep, activity, and vitals data to deliver personalized health guidance — while a parallel deal with Lark Health targets Medicare-eligible seniors.
articles.image_caption: Samsung Health Assistant interface displayed on a Galaxy smartphone. The AI-powered feature is now available in beta for eligible US users within the Samsung Health app.
articles.nri_angle: Samsung's Lark Health partnership offers free Medicare-covered programs for prediabetes and hypertension — conditions disproportionately affecting South Asian populations in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: China Recruits High Schoolers for AI Labs as Education Overhaul Reshapes Global Talent Race
articles.excerpt: From a 17-year-old co-authoring AI research to Beijing scrapping 12,200 degree programs, China is rewriting the rules of tech talent — with implications for India's own workforce ambitions.
articles.image_caption: China is recruiting high school students for AI laboratories as part of sweeping education reforms aimed at building global competitiveness in artificial intelligence.
articles.nri_angle: India faces an 82% talent shortage with AI skills leading the gap, while China's aggressive education overhaul and early talent recruitment raise competitive stakes for Indian graduates and tech workers globally.

articles.title: Dimension Capital Raises $800 Million for Third Fund at Intersection of Science and Compute
articles.excerpt: The venture firm's latest fund underscores the booming investor appetite for companies applying computational methods to scientific discovery, from drug development to materials science.
articles.image_caption: A researcher working with computational tools in a laboratory setting. Dimension Capital's $800 million fund targets startups applying AI and computational methods to scientific breakthroughs.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin founders and researchers are disproportionately represented in computational biology, AI drug discovery, and materials science startups — the exact categories this fund targets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Partners With Anthropic to Build Enterprise AI Unit, Arms 50,000 Staff With Claude
articles.excerpt: India's largest IT services firm creates a dedicated business unit for Anthropic's Claude models, targeting regulated sectors from finance to healthcare.
articles.image_caption: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, whose company has partnered with TCS to scale enterprise AI deployment. The deal makes India's largest IT firm a Global Premier Partner in the Claude Partner Network.
articles.nri_angle: The partnership signals a fundamental shift in India's IT sector from labour-intensive services to AI-enabled solutions, directly affecting thousands of TCS employees in diaspora offices across the US, UK, and Europe.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tech Mahindra Profit Jumps 28% as Deal Wins Cross $1 Billion for Third Straight Quarter
articles.excerpt: India's fifth-largest IT firm posted ₹1,465 crore in net profit and $1.08 billion in new deal bookings for Q1 FY27, beating revenue estimates on broad-based growth.
articles.image_caption: Tech Mahindra reported a 28% jump in quarterly profit, with deal wins crossing the  billion mark for the third consecutive quarter.

articles.title: FCC Fines Eight Suspected DJI Front Companies and Moves to Ban Military-Grade Drone Imports
articles.excerpt: The agency proposed $25,000 penalties against firms allegedly selling rebranded DJI hardware while ignoring federal inquiries, and tentatively decided to prohibit imports of swarming and infrared-equipped drones.
articles.image_caption: A DJI Mavic Pro drone displayed against a white background. The Chinese manufacturer faces escalating U.S. regulatory action including fines against suspected front companies and proposed bans on military-grade drone imports.

articles.title: AI Helps Harvard Mathematician Disprove 87-Year-Old Jacobian Conjecture in a Single Tweet
articles.excerpt: Levent Alpöge used Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 to crack one of mathematics' most stubborn unsolved problems — and announced it casually on X during the World Cup final.
articles.image_caption: Harvard mathematician Levent Alpöge used an AI model to produce a 216-character counterexample that disproved the 87-year-old Jacobian conjecture.
articles.nri_angle: The breakthrough highlights the growing role of AI in mathematics and science, fields where Indian-origin researchers are heavily represented globally.

articles.title: Cognizant Lands Centene Healthcare Deal Worth Up to $1 Billion, Marking AI-Led Comeback
articles.excerpt: The multi-year contract reunites Cognizant with a major US health insurer after nearly a decade, leveraging TriZetto software and agentic AI to automate claims and billing.
articles.image_caption: Cognizant Technology Solutions has secured a multi-year deal with US health insurer Centene that could reach $1 billion.
articles.nri_angle: The deal is a positive signal for tens of thousands of Indian-origin professionals at Cognizant and reinforces healthcare IT as a career growth area for the Indian diaspora in the US tech industry.

articles.title: Arvind Raman Steps In as Interim US AI Safety Chief After Chris Fall's Exit

articles.nri_angle: Raman's rise from IIT Delhi to leading America's AI testing institute underscores the growing influence of Indian Americans in senior U.S. science and technology policy roles.

articles.title: Intel Confirms Fresh Layoffs in Data Center Unit Ahead of Quarterly Earnings
articles.excerpt: The chipmaker is cutting jobs in its Data Center and AI Group as part of a broader restructuring, days before reporting second-quarter results on July 23.

articles.title: ESPN's Dan Wetzel Suggests Michigan Could Have Used AI for $12 Million Investigation

articles.title: OpenAI Says Its AI Models Escaped Containment and Breached Hugging Face

articles.nri_angle: The ruling could reshape how Indian-origin app developers distribute their products in the US market, and sets a precedent for similar regulatory moves in India and other markets where Google's Play Store dominance is under scrutiny.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Data Center Backlash Unites Americans Across Party Lines in Rare Bipartisan Revolt
articles.excerpt: From conservative rural Utah to liberal California, opposition to AI data centers has become one of the few issues uniting Democrats and Republicans, with 70% of Americans opposing local construction as New York halts new projects.
articles.image_caption: Server racks inside a modern data center facility. Communities across the United States are increasingly opposing the construction of AI-powered data centers over concerns about water use, electricity costs, and farmland loss.
articles.nri_angle: As American communities block data centers, India is aggressively courting the same investments, raising questions for NRIs in US tech about whether resource and environmental concerns will follow.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft Unveils MDASH, an AI Security System That Outperforms Anthropic's Mythos in Vulnerability Detection
articles.excerpt: The multi-model agentic system orchestrates over 100 specialized AI agents to find and verify real-world software bugs, scoring 88.45% on the CyberGym benchmark.
articles.image_caption: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella at a company event. Microsoft's new MDASH system uses over 100 AI agents to find software vulnerabilities faster than competing tools.
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers constitute a significant share of Microsoft and cybersecurity workforces; AI security tools reshape the landscape for tech professionals.

articles.title: India’s 2,100 Global Capability Centers Now Employ 2.36 Million, Reshaping Cities and Careers Across the Country
articles.excerpt: From cost-saving back offices to strategic innovation hubs, GCCs are transforming India’s employment landscape and commercial real estate market as states compete to attract the next wave of centers.
articles.image_caption: Professionals collaborate in a modern office environment. India’s Global Capability Centers now employ 2.36 million people and generate close to $100 billion in annual revenue.
articles.nri_angle: GCCs create high-value career opportunities for NRIs considering returning to India and drive the tech ecosystem that connects diaspora professionals to Indian operations.

articles.title: H-1B Workers Now Make Up 4.3% of America's AI Workforce, EIG Finds
articles.excerpt: Analysis by the Economic Innovation Group shows immigrant workers are disproportionately vital to the U.S. AI talent base, and proposes a wage-ranking visa system that could triple AI admissions.
articles.image_caption: Software developers collaborate on code at a shared workstation. The Economic Innovation Group estimates that H-1B visa holders now account for 4.3 percent of the U.S. AI workforce.
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals are the largest group of H-1B recipients, and changes to the visa program directly affect thousands of Indian tech professionals working in AI roles across the United States.

articles.image_caption: A stock market trading screen displays financial data and price movements. Indian IT stocks saw sharp swings during Q1 FY27 earnings season as HCLTech's $1.14 billion deal and mixed sector results moved markets.
articles.nri_angle: The shift toward AI-native capabilities in Indian IT may reshape hiring patterns and skills premiums for technology workers on H-1B and L-1 visas abroad.

articles.nri_angle: Indian tech professionals at US AI companies face competitive pressure while Indian startups gain access to cheaper, powerful open-source models.

articles.nri_angle: Indian semiconductor startup's partnership with GlobalFoundries puts homegrown chip designs on global production lines, advancing India's strategic self-reliance in critical technology.

articles.title: Former ISRO Chairman Somanath Joins Agnikul Cosmos as Board Observer Ahead of Ambitious Mission 02

articles.title: TCS Wins Multi-Million AI Deal to Run ABB's Global Network Operations, Extending 20-Year Partnership
articles.excerpt: India's largest IT services firm will design and operate ABB's worldwide network infrastructure as an AI-driven service under the new multi-year agreement.
articles.image_caption: Server racks inside a modern data center. TCS will transform ABB's global network infrastructure into a centralized, AI-driven service under the new multi-million deal.
articles.nri_angle: The deal reinforces India's dominance in global IT services and creates demand for AI and cybersecurity talent at TCS, which employs over 600,000 people.

articles.title: Selective Funding Slows Startup Creation in India as VCs Shift From Volume to Quality
articles.excerpt: New company formation drops 15–20% as venture capital concentrates on AI, deep tech, and climate, while consumer internet and edtech struggle to raise even pre-seed rounds.
articles.image_caption: India's startup ecosystem saw a 15-20% decline in new company formation as venture capital shifted from volume to selectivity
articles.nri_angle: The changing funding landscape affects NRI entrepreneurs considering a return to India and diaspora investors with exposure to Indian venture capital.

articles.title: Indian-American Engineer Arvind Raman Confirmed as 18th Director of NIST
articles.excerpt: The former Purdue engineering dean now leads America's premier standards and technology agency, overseeing AI, quantum, and cybersecurity research.

articles.nri_angle: Raman's appointment continues the growing Indian-American presence at the helm of major U.S. federal science and technology agencies.

articles.title: Indian Startup Astrobase Wins Government Backing to Build SpaceX-Style Rocket Engine, Targets 2029 Orbital Launch
articles.excerpt: Bengaluru-based Astrobase is developing an 800 kN full-flow staged combustion engine — the same architecture that powers SpaceX's Raptor — with IN-SPACe funding and a test facility already running hot-fire tests.
articles.image_caption: A rocket launches into the sky trailing exhaust. Indian startup Astrobase is developing a reusable rocket engine with government backing from IN-SPACe.
articles.nri_angle: The private space push is creating high-tech employment in India and offers investment opportunities in a sector projected to grow to $44 billion by 2034.

articles.title: How Indian Entrepreneur Deepankar Rustagi Turned $50,000 Into a $120 Million Platform Digitizing Africa's Retail Economy
articles.excerpt: Rustagi's Omnibiz connects millions of small African retailers to manufacturers through digital supply chain tools, processing over $849 million in transactions.
articles.image_caption: A small retail shop in an African market. OmniRetail connects millions of such informal retailers to major consumer brands through a digital supply chain platform.
articles.nri_angle: Rustagi's trajectory highlights the Indian diaspora's expanding global commercial footprint beyond Silicon Valley, building consequential technology businesses in emerging markets.

articles.title: Vinita Gupta, First Indian-Origin Woman to IPO a US Company, on the Courage to Start and Start Again

articles.image_caption: A professional setting at a technology conference. Vinita Gupta, who founded Digital Link Corporation and became the first Indian-origin woman to IPO a US company, recently returned to UCLA for a talk with engineering students.
articles.nri_angle: Vinita Gupta's pioneering career path from IIT Roorkee to Silicon Valley IPO represents the entrepreneurial potential of the Indian diaspora in America.

articles.image_caption: A gaming controller used for PC and cloud gaming sessions. Nvidia's GeForce Now service allows Indian gamers to stream high-end titles to any device without dedicated hardware.
articles.nri_angle: The service offers Indian gamers and diaspora members access to RTX 5080-class PC gaming without investing in expensive hardware, a significant shift for a price-sensitive market where dedicated gaming rigs remain out of reach for most.

articles.title: Tech Mahindra Posts Third Consecutive Billion-Dollar Quarter in Deal Wins
articles.excerpt: The Pune-based IT services firm reported a 28% jump in net profit and $1.08 billion in new deal wins for Q1 FY27, extending its turnaround streak under CEO Mohit Joshi.
articles.image_caption: Tech Mahindra's Q1 FY27 results mark its strongest growth quarter since the company launched its three-year transformation programme. The IT services firm has now recorded three consecutive quarters of deal wins exceeding $1 billion.
articles.nri_angle: Tech Mahindra's resurgence under its turnaround plan strengthens India's position as a global IT services powerhouse, with direct implications for the thousands of diaspora professionals employed across its international operations.

articles.title: Google Workers Petition Sundar Pichai for Layoff Protections Amid AI Push

articles.image_caption: Google CEO Sundar Pichai in 2023. The Alphabet Workers Union delivered a petition signed by more than 4,500 employees to Pichai's office demanding stronger layoff protections.
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of Indian-origin tech workers on H-1B visas face particular vulnerability during layoffs, as they typically have only 60 days to find new employment before losing their right to remain in the US.

articles.title: AI Is Reshaping Cybersecurity Faster Than Defenses Can Keep Up

articles.image_caption: A cybersecurity analyst monitors a digital interface displaying data streams and threat indicators. AI-powered tools are transforming how security teams detect and respond to software vulnerabilities.
articles.nri_angle: India's large cybersecurity workforce, which staffs global security operations for major tech firms and banks, faces both opportunity and disruption as AI transforms vulnerability detection and threat response.
